knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=-3x^{2}+4x
$$

at the point $\left(-1,-7\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-3x^{2}+4x$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-6x+4
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-1,-7\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-1)&=-6\left(-1\right)+4\\
&=6+4\\
&=10
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(10\right)}\\
&=-\frac{1}{10}
\end{aligned}
$$
